validation_policy.local: Compile/import, focused static checks, selector collection, and each task's exact selectors only; broad local suites are not the default.
progression: static and import checks for the changed slice

validation_policy.reuse: Reuse a green layer only when candidate, changed files and tests, settings digest, selector set, tool and runtime identity, environment, and prior outcome are exactly equal.
validation_policy.failure_gate: Every red is classified product, test, infrastructure, environment, mixed, or unknown before any correction. Only an exclusive product inventory may enter Fix.
validation_policy.terminal_ci: One unsharded Python 3.12 suite plus only independent quality/package, browser, interpreter-import, OS-boundary, security, and no-egress validations. No pytest shards and no compatibility join job.

delivery.test_count_policy: report the behavioral result; no arbitrary count or line ceiling

loop.py, tp.py, host hooks, and the Design host role are the single high-fan-in lifecycle and dispatch composition boundary

test_contract.freshness: Candidate, run, stage instance, settings digest, selector set, evidence digest, runtime, and receipt schema are bound.
test_contract.severed_edges: Uncollectable selectors, missing consumers, unverifiable evidence, stale candidate identity, unknown class, or mixed inventory holds correction authority.
test_contract.fixtures: Only serialized or external interface changes require same-slice fixtures; in-process interfaces require a real consumer journey.

criteria: One canonical failure schema is produced for Build, Evaluate, and CI observations, binds the full working candidate, and fails closed on missing or unverifiable evidence.

The quality receipt collects exact selectors and proves static checks, exact behavior, producer consumers, freshness, semantic severed edges, and applicable fixture co-change through one canonical progression.

test_contract.freshness: Every manifest and event binds repository, run, stage instance, full working candidate, settings digest, source fingerprint, and schema.
test_contract.severed_edges: Missing class directories, manifest mismatch, unreadable evidence, or target overlap in either direction blocks cleanup atomically.
test_contract.fixtures: Filesystem fixtures cover private permissions, no-follow creation, symlinks, hardlinks, foreign runs, ambiguous ownership, every terminal outcome, and recovery.

criteria: One private run-adjacent manifest owns separate dashboard, dependency-graphs, telemetry, agent-activity, validation, cleanup, and retro artifact classes without becoming lifecycle state.
Cleanup prevalidates the complete deletion set, refuses unsafe or ambiguous ownership, preserves durable evidence, and proves zero exact-owned leaks on all terminal outcomes.

test_contract.freshness: Settings, catalog, requirement, decomposition, graph, candidate, and source fingerprints change the team and stage-graph receipts.
test_contract.severed_edges: Skipping decomposition, forcing a fixed list, exceeding the sixteen-worker cap, accepting unsafe scope, or reusing a prior-run graph fails exact behavior.
test_contract.fixtures: Canonical settings are prepopulated with working defaults; safe overrides change behavior without code edits and governance-weakening overrides fail closed.

criteria: The default settings file is complete yet simple, treats sixteen as a Design cap rather than a target, and supports dynamic routes and safe overrides without source changes.
Every Design entry performs current-run decomposition before lens selection and seals the current graph for consumers.

test_contract.freshness: The complete visible binding contains run, requirement, stage, revision, settings digest, authority receipt, snapshot fingerprint, graph receipt, and publication epoch.
test_contract.severed_edges: Workspace mutation after snapshot, delayed prior-stage publication, missing host acknowledgement, degraded graph, or prior-run receipt keeps actions inert and cannot replace current head.
test_contract.fixtures: Browser fixtures exercise current Design and Plan graphs, responsive 390 and 768 pixel layouts, computed styles, nonzero geometry, accessible SVG text, offline file preview, and action safety.

criteria: All dashboard and native surfaces render the same sealed current-run graph and full provenance binding, and a delayed or unacknowledged publication cannot become current.
The graph is visibly nonzero with real computed styles and geometry on desktop and compact layouts; static file previews remain truthful and read-only.

test_contract.freshness: Every dispatch and evaluator attempt is attributable to one run, candidate, worker, stage, outcome, usage source, and receipt digest.
test_contract.severed_edges: A nonempty run with missing attempt usage cannot claim measured totals or zero; sealing blocks or reports attributable unavailable.
test_contract.fixtures: Lifecycle ledgers cover measured usage, unavailable host usage, evaluator identities, cancellations, interruptions, handoffs, and terminal retries.

criteria: Terminal metrics preserve measured or attributable unavailable usage, evaluator identities and outcomes, and never coerce missing telemetry to zero.
Retro consumes the sealed terminal ledger before cleanup and reports baseline, target, and achieved wall-clock, CI, parallelism, cleanup, portfolio, and token metrics.

acceptance_refs: A fresh governed Design run shows the active requirement and a visible nonzero dependency graph derived from the same canonical snapshot.
Automatic decomposition completes before dynamic Design lens selection and settings changes alter actual selection without source edits.
Every failure has a complete typed record before repair; non-product and unknown failures cannot enter product Fix.
Retro reports measured token totals or explicit unavailable status, retains evaluator identities, and never converts missing usage to zero.
Behavioral journey tests cover the public producers and consumers; source-shape, byte-identity, stale-history, and ceremonial tests are removed.

test_contract.freshness: Repository, run, stage instance, requirement, full working candidate, settings, catalog, team plan, graph, authority revision, worker attempt, output, and terminal set are jointly bound.
test_contract.severed_edges: A settings-only change must alter actual assignment where policy demands it; any missing, duplicate, self-attested, stale, foreign-host, or unlogged worker prevents Design completion.
test_contract.fixtures: Public journeys use real host-dispatch adapters and lifecycle hooks; they do not accept a generated plan or self-digested result as execution proof.

criteria: Every Taskplane flow pins one validated settings and active-run identity before effects, automatically decomposes before Design selection, dispatches exactly the selected worker set through the host, waits once, and conserves host-issued terminal receipts.
Every worker assignment, start, progress, attention, cancellation, interruption, handoff, usage, evidence reference, and terminal outcome is durably logged beside the run.
Build cannot enter Evaluate without a current quality receipt; Evaluate cannot enter correction without a typed failure inventory; only exclusive product failure opens Fix.
Cross-host handoff preserves portable role and artifact references while rejecting absolute, foreign-run, stale-candidate, or replayed authority.

acceptance_refs: Dashboard publications, graph and dependency evidence, telemetry, and every agent activity log are stored as separate durable artifact classes beside the run and survive every cleanup outcome.

test_contract.freshness: The journey proves all artifact references and activity events bind the same active run and exact candidate.
test_contract.severed_edges: Remove one class publisher, one worker event, or one cleanup exclusion and the public lifecycle proof fails.
test_contract.fixtures: Temporary repositories model success, failure, cancellation, interruption, handoff, timeout, recovery, unsafe aliases, and foreign evidence.

criteria: The public governed lifecycle creates all seven separate durable artifact classes, logs every worker outcome, removes only exact-owned ephemera, preserves evidence, and verifies zero leaks for every terminal path.

acceptance_refs: Behavioral journey tests cover the public producers and consumers; source-shape, byte-identity, stale-history, and ceremonial tests are removed.

test_contract.freshness: The portfolio records current collected cases, files, families, protected contracts, replacement journeys, fixture consumers, and evidence revision without imposing count or line ratchets.
test_contract.severed_edges: Every removal requires current-product authority and retained semantic proof; source text, line count, byte identity, fixture existence, historical acceptance, and workflow job names cannot stand alone.
test_contract.fixtures: Delete unconsumed or stale fixtures with their tests; keep fixtures only where serialized compatibility, portability, security, release, or public behavior consumes them.

criteria: Every tracked test file is classified for current-product value; all identified shape-only, byte-identity-as-correctness, line/count ratchet, stale-history, duplicate, stale-fixture, and ceremonial families are removed or rewritten after replacement proof.

Security and authority boundaries, exact-owned cleanup, portability, release version/tag provenance, real browser behavior, current-run graph provenance, typed failure routing, and truthful metrics remain protected.

acceptance_refs: GitHub Actions runs one unsharded authoritative Python 3.12 suite plus only genuinely independent validations.

test_contract.freshness: Each direct job receipt binds the exact candidate, settings, command, runtime, environment, and artifact manifest; no synthetic join rebrands job results.
test_contract.severed_edges: Adding a pytest shard, overlapping compatibility tests, a branch-protection join pseudo-test, missing typed red receipt, or missing always-cleanup fails the journey.
test_contract.fixtures: Workflow behavior is parsed and executed through the runner plan; raw YAML strings or check names alone are not acceptance evidence.

criteria: GitHub Actions runs the complete pytest inventory exactly once on Python 3.12, in parallel only with genuinely independent validations, and exposes no join job disguised as tests.
Every red cell publishes a typed failure and durable evidence before enforcement; cleanup runs on every outcome and cannot target run artifacts.

test_contract.freshness: Version, release candidate, protected-main CI, archive members, installation probe, and provenance are bound to the merged candidate.
test_contract.severed_edges: Omitting a new runtime owner, settings, hook, skill, artifact schema, version surface, or install behavior blocks packaging.
test_contract.fixtures: Package tests inspect members, schemas, versions, provenance, installation, and executable behavior; archive byte identity is not treated as correctness unless reproducibility is explicitly declared.

criteria: The next version is consistent across release and marketplace surfaces, both packages include all new runtime owners and canonical defaults, and an installed fresh package executes the governed public journey.
The final merged candidate, authoritative green CI, installed version, marketplace archive, and complete Retro evidence ZIP share one auditable provenance chain.
